title: Dividing a Unit Fraction by a Whole Number

steps.body: Dividing a unit fraction by a whole number cuts an already-small piece into smaller ones: one fourth shared three ways gives twelfths.
steps.narration: Dividing a unit fraction by a whole number cuts an already-small piece into smaller ones: one fourth shared three ways gives twelfths.

widget.prompt: One fourth is about to be shared 3 ways. Build that fourth as twelfths first.
widget.successFeedback: 3/12 — the same fourth, now cut into twelfths, so the three-way share is one twelfth each.
widget.lowFeedback: That build is SHORTER than 3/12 — either shade more pieces or make each piece larger until the lengths match.
widget.highFeedback: That build is LONGER than 3/12 — either shade fewer pieces or make each piece smaller until the lengths match.

commonFractions.feedback: A single twelfth is ONE of the three shares, not the whole fourth being shared.
3/4 is three of the original fourths, far more than the single fourth being shared.

predict.prompt: Sharing 1/4 three ways, does the denominator grow or shrink?
predict.reveal: More cuts means more pieces in the whole, so the number naming the piece size rises.

cml.actionGoal: Ask what is being cut and how big each piece is, then count the pieces for g5fd unit by whole.
invariants: Division and fractions are the same act seen twice: sharing a wholes among b people gives a/b, and dividing BY a piece asks how many of it fit, which is why g5fd unit by whole produces a larger answer when the divisor is under one.
misconceptions: Reading "divide by 1/4" as "take a quarter of", reporting a remainder when the leftover could be shared, or shrinking the pieces when only their count should change.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the divisor grew past one, would the answer become larger or smaller than the dividend?

widget.prompt: Compute 5 × 5 — the denominator you get when one fifth is shared 5 ways.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding the two numbers does not cut anything; sharing 5 ways multiplies the piece count.
5 is the denominator BEFORE the sharing; each piece is about to get smaller.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Ask what is being cut and what size the pieces are; the count of pieces is the answer.
